band_change_evidence_test.detail: NOT APPLICABLE. Assessed 43.1 and published 48.4 are both inside the Functional band (41-60). No band boundary is crossed, so the band-crossing sourcing bar is not engaged. Filed on the MAGNITUDE trigger only (|delta| 5.3 >= 5.0). NOTE FOR THE REVIEWER: 43.1 sits only 2.1 points above the Developing boundary at 41.0. Any further downward movement would engage the band-crossing bar, which would require >=2 independent sources with >=1 at tier >=4 EXCLUDING self-published corporate material. No tier-4-or-above source on this dispute was located in this cycle, so that bar is NOT currently met and a band crossing would not presently be filable.

scoring_convention: Absence of disclosure scores 2, never 1. A score of 1 requires positive documented evidence of a specific failure. Absence is not evidence of harm.

anti_false_positive_screening.baseline_provenance: Published 48.4 with ACC 2.5 and INT 2.5. rotation-state records last_assessed 2026-06-21, last_change_proposal null. APPLIED_CHANGES.md contains no Starbucks entry. The published Accountability and Integrity scores of 2.5 already partly encode the labour dispute, which is why this proposal does not treat the five-year bargaining failure as an entirely new finding.
anti_false_positive_screening.directionality: Entity surfaced on within-window evidence that is largely NOT its own conduct. This proposal is a DOWNGRADE and rests only on the residue that IS company conduct. Direction matches the retained evidence.
anti_false_positive_screening.attribution_exclusions: THE BOYCOTT IS NOT SCORED. Starbucks Workers United announcing a boycott on 2026-08-25, the AFL-CIO joining, and the 25,000-member Chicago Teachers Union voting to join on 2026-08-26 are acts of OTHER ORGANISATIONS — a campaign against the company, not company conduct. All three are excluded from scoring. Only Starbucks own conduct is scored: the unconcluded first contract with a unit organised in late 2021, and the company's own public statements.
anti_false_positive_screening.evidence_deliberately_excluded: UNION-ASSERTED UNFAIR-LABOR-PRACTICE COUNTS WERE NOT RELIED ON. Labor Notes reports "550 still unresolved"; Starbucks Workers United's own site reports "more than 700"; other advocacy sources cite "more than 400 labor law violations" found by administrative law judges. These come from a party to the dispute, they contradict each other by 150 or more, and none was verifiable against a primary National Labor Relations Board record. NO subdimension rests on them. Had they been used the movement would have been substantially larger.
anti_false_positive_screening.countervailing_evidence_credited: A 2026 United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit decision vacated an NLRB unfair labor practice ruling against Starbucks — the adjudicated record is contested, not settled against the company. Starbucks provides health coverage to part-time workers and tuition support; Boundaries is HELD at 3.0 and five subdimensions are scored 3 on these grounds.
anti_false_positive_screening.measures_absence_note: No subdimension in this assessment is scored 1. The movement measures documented conduct — an unconcluded five-year negotiation and the company's public statements about it — not absence of disclosure.

key_evidence: Starbucks and Starbucks Workers United have not concluded a first contract for a bargaining unit that organised in late 2021 — approaching five years. Verified via CNBC and the Texarkana Gazette wire report, not only union sources.
Starbucks spokesperson Jaci Anderson: "As we have always been, we're committed to engaging in productive bargaining." The company also stated it had seen no impact to its business from the boycott.
THE BOYCOTT ITSELF IS EXCLUDED AS THIRD-PARTY CONDUCT. A campaign against a company is not something the company did. This removes most of the evidence the scanner surfaced.
The largest single subdimension movement is AC5 (follow-through) from 3 to 2: engagement that has run since late 2021 without reaching resolution.
CREDITED AGAINST THE MOVEMENT: part-time health coverage and tuition support are genuine structural benefits; Boundaries is held at 3.0 and no subdimension is scored 1.

evidence.claim: The union's core staffing demand, which the company has not matched — used for proportionality, not as a finding against the company.

evidence.claim: The union submitted a written contract proposal in March 2026 and the company returned to the bargaining table — credited under Perspective-Taking.

notes: FLAG FOR REVIEW — NOT A RECOMMENDED DOWNGRADE. Filed on the magnitude trigger (-5.3); no band crossing. THE ROUTING REASON IS EVIDENTIAL WEIGHT, NOT DOUBT ABOUT THE FACTS. Once the boycott, the AFL-CIO endorsement and the Chicago Teachers Union vote are correctly EXCLUDED as third-party conduct — a campaign against Starbucks is not something Starbucks did — the genuinely new in-window company conduct amounts to another month passing without a contract and one spokesperson statement. That is thin evidence for a 5.3-point move. The magnitude rests principally on the CUMULATIVE five-year bargaining failure, which is not new and is already partly reflected in the published Accountability and Integrity scores of 2.5. A FOUNDER MAY REASONABLY CONCLUDE THIS IS BETTER HANDLED AS A CONFIRMATION WITH A DOWNWARD WATCH FLAG, and that conclusion would be defensible on this file. EVIDENCE DELIBERATELY NOT USED: all union-asserted unfair-labor-practice counts (550 / 700+ / 400+ violations) — party-sourced, mutually contradictory, unverifiable against a primary NLRB record. Using them would have produced a larger movement on weaker evidence. COUNTERVAILING EVIDENCE CREDITED: a 2026 Fifth Circuit decision vacated an NLRB ruling against Starbucks; part-time health coverage and tuition support hold Boundaries at 3.0. CONFIDENCE LOW on evidence quality — the primary gap is the absence of any primary National Labor Relations Board record. This is NOT a self-veto; the figure is internally sound and may be applied if the founder judges the cumulative reading correct.
